s0202.literal: Now on a sudden, moreover because those in charge were inattentive in drafting the text, they would withdraw an edict already issued and seize a benefaction already poured out; your servant's foolish heart privately deems this unacceptable.
s0202.idiomatic: If, overnight, careless wording by those in charge is now taken as grounds to rescind a promulgated edict and claw back a grant already made, I humbly submit that cannot be justified.

s0203.idiomatic: The throne approved the proposal by edict.

s0204.literal: Within the Yuankang years, he was transferred to be Friend of the Prince of Wu.
s0204.idiomatic: During the Yuankang era he was appointed Companion to the Prince of Wu.

s0205.literal: At the time Xun Yi was compiling the New Rites; he caused Yu to discuss what was right and wrong, and afterward put it into practice.
s0205.idiomatic: While Xun Yi was drafting the New Rites, he had Yu review its strengths and flaws before implementation.

s0206.literal: When Empress Yuan died, Du Yu memorialized: "The liang'an regulations come from high antiquity; therefore Gaozong has no wording about wearing mourning, and the text only says he 'did not speak.'
s0206.idiomatic: On the death of Empress Yuan, Du Yu argued: "The liang'an observance reaches back to remote antiquity, which is why the inscription for Gaozong says nothing about donning mourning—only that he kept silence."

s0207.literal: Han Wendi limited it to thirty-six days.
s0207.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han fixed the period at thirty-six days.

s0208.literal: From the Wei house downward, they took the ji sacrifice as the regulating node.
s0208.idiomatic: From the Wei dynasty on, the ji sacrifice marked the ritual cutoff.

s0209.literal: The heir apparent with the state forms one body; by principle it is fitting to release the garments; at the end of wailing immediately remove them.
s0209.idiomatic: The crown prince is one with the body politic; he should leave off mourning and lay aside his garb as soon as the final wailing ends.

s0210.literal: Yu answered Du Yu in a letter, saying: "Tang called it 'stemming music,' Yin called it 'credence in dimness'—each raised an affair to make a name; it was not that after burial there was a special reduction in mourning."
s0210.idiomatic: Yu wrote back to Du Yu: "The Tang spoke of silencing music, the Yin of 'credence in dimness'—each named a practice; neither implies a different rule depending on whether burial was already past."

s0211.literal: From the Zhou house onward, they called it mourning garments.
s0211.idiomatic: Since Zhou times it has been termed mourning dress.

s0212.literal: Mourning garments: by garments they displayed mourning.
s0212.idiomatic: Mourning dress is meant to make bereavement visible.

s0213.literal: Now the one who is emperor in one day has ten thousand offices; the weight of the heir apparent's supervision and nurturing—with regard to it, it is fitting to truncate the rites; when burial is finished remove the garments; changing the system penetrates principle; hand down the norm for the future—why must one attach it to antiquity and make old Confucians wrangle!
s0213.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven faces a myriad decisions each day, and the crown prince bears a heavy supervisory charge; it is right to shorten the mourning cycle and end it at burial—adjusting the rules accords with reason and sets a precedent for later ages. Why bind the matter to archaic precedent and set aged classicists at odds?

s0214.literal: When the imperial great-grandson Shang died, the responsible offices memorialized 'imperial garments: zi-cui for one year.'
s0214.idiomatic: On the death of Imperial Great-grandson Shang, the authorities requested that the emperor observe one year of zi-cui mourning.

s0215.literal: An edict ordered the erudites to deliberate.
s0215.idiomatic: An edict directed the academicians to debate the issue.

s0216.literal: Yu said: "When the heir apparent was born, he was raised with the rites of an adult; then the principle of 'early death' is removed."
s0216.idiomatic: Yu said: "The heir apparent was welcomed with ceremonies due a grown successor, so the category of a child's untimely death no longer applies."

s0217.literal: The imperial grandson likewise embodies the ruler and transmits the weight; because of the completion of status the garments are complete, not because of years.
s0217.idiomatic: The imperial grandson likewise stands for the sovereign and shoulders the succession; mourning follows from his station, not from his age.

s0219.literal: Yu also debated the jade chariot and the matter of the two altars of soil; see the Record of Carriages and Robes.
s0219.idiomatic: Yu also argued the cases of the jade state carriage and the twin earth altars; see Carriages and Regalia.

s0220.literal: Afterward he passed through Palace Library Supervisor and Commandant of the Guards, following Emperor Hui in visiting Chang'an.
s0220.idiomatic: He later served as Director of the Palace Library and Commandant of the Guards, accompanying Emperor Hui to Chang'an.

s0221.literal: When the eastern army came to welcome them, the hundred officials fled and scattered; thus he drifted in destitution between Hu and Du, turned and entered the southern mountains, provisions cut off, hunger extreme; he gathered acorns and ate them.
s0221.idiomatic: When the eastern relief force arrived, officials scattered in panic; he wandered destitute between Hu and Du, fled into the southern hills, starved when food ran out, and subsisted on gathered acorns.

s0222.literal: Afterward he was able to return to Luoyang; he passed through Grand Coachman and Chamberlain for Ceremonials.
s0222.idiomatic: He eventually returned to Luoyang and held the posts of Grand Coachman and Minister of Ceremonial.

s0223.literal: At the time Emperor Huai personally performed the suburban sacrifice.
s0223.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Huai personally offered the suburban sacrifice to Heaven.

s0224.literal: From Yuankang onward, he had not personally performed suburban sacrifices; rites and observances loosened and were abandoned.
s0224.idiomatic: Since the Yuankang era the suburban rites had not been performed in person by the sovereign, and the ritual program had lapsed.

s0225.literal: Yu examined and corrected old canons; ritual implements were bright and clear.
s0225.idiomatic: Yu collated the old regulations so that insignia and ritual gear stood in good order.

s0226.literal: When Luoyang-the-capital was wild and chaotic, theft ran rampant; people hungry ate one another.
s0226.idiomatic: When the capital fell into chaos, banditry ran rife and famine drove people to cannibalism.

s0227.literal: Yu by nature was clean and poor; thus because of hunger he died.
s0227.idiomatic: Yu had always lived in austere poverty and died of starvation.

s0228.literal: Yu compiled the Monograph on Literature in four rolls, annotated the Accounts Resolved concerning the Three Aides of the Capital, also compiled ancient literary pieces, gathering by category and dividing into thirty rolls, named them Collection of Genres by Current, for each he wrote a discourse; phrasing and principle were apt and fitting, and the age valued him.
s0228.idiomatic: Yu wrote the four-scroll Treatise on Literature, annotated the Capital Region Records, and arranged ancient belles-lettres into thirty scrolls by genre under the title Collected Genres of Writing, appending a critical essay to each—his contemporaries prized the balance of diction and argument.

s0229.literal: Yu was good at observing the dark celestial images; once he said to a friend: "Now the realm below is about to be chaotic; a state for fleeing calamity—is it not only the Liang region!"
s0229.idiomatic: Yu was skilled at reading the stars; he once told a friend, "The empire is sliding into turmoil—for a bolt-hole, surely nothing rivals the northwest."

s0230.literal: His nature loved gentlemen; for those who had memorial-recommendations, he always composed their wording.
s0230.idiomatic: He delighted in promoting scholars and habitually drafted the memorials for those he recommended.

s0231.literal: The Grandee of the Eastern March, Taishu Guang, was pivot-pure and clear in disputation; Guang discoursed at length; Yu could not answer;
s0231.idiomatic: Taishu Guang of Dongping was quick and eloquent in debate; in extemporaneous argument Yu could not match him—

s0232.literal: Yu with the brush; Guang could not answer;
s0232.idiomatic: but when brushwork was the test, Guang had no reply.

s0233.literal: Mutually they sneered and laughed; it was confused in the world, they say.
s0233.idiomatic: They traded jibes to the amusement of their contemporaries, or so the story goes.

s0235.literal: Shu Xi, courtesy Guangwei, a man of Yuancheng in Yangping, was a descendant of Han Heir Apparent Grand Tutor Shu Guang.
s0235.idiomatic: Shu Xi, style Guangwei, a native of Yuancheng in Yangping commandery, traced his line to Shu Guang, Grand Tutor to the Han heir apparent.

s0236.literal: At the end of Wang Mang, Guang's great-grandson Mengda fled disaster, from Donghai moved dwelling south of Mount Shalu, thereby removing the 'foot' of Shu, thus changed surname.
s0236.idiomatic: Near the close of Wang Mang's reign, Guang's great-grandson Mengda fled the turmoil, moving from the eastern seaboard to the south of Mount Shalu and dropping the lower component of the character Shu, whence the family surname changed.

s0237.idiomatic: His grandfather Hun had been Administrator of Longxi.

s0238.literal: Father Kan, Administrator of Fengyi; both had reputation.
s0238.idiomatic: His father Kan was Administrator of Fengyi; both men enjoyed repute.

s0239.literal: Xi learned broadly and heard much; together with elder brother Qiu both were known by name.
s0239.idiomatic: Shu Xi was erudite and widely read; he and his elder brother Qiu were celebrated alike.

s0240.literal: In youth he roamed the national school; someone asked Erudite Cao Zhi, saying: "Who today are the fond-of-learning ones?"
s0240.idiomatic: As a youth he studied at the imperial academy. Someone asked Academician Cao Zhi, "Who in our day are the true scholars?"

s0241.literal: Zhi said: "Yangping's Shu Guangwei is fond of learning without weariness; people cannot reach him."
s0241.idiomatic: Cao Zhi replied, "Shu Guangwei of Yangping—his love of learning never flags; no one can equal him."

s0242.literal: He returned to his village; was inspected Filially Incorrupt; was raised Abundant Talent; all he did not go to.
s0242.idiomatic: He went home, was nominated Filial and Incorrupt and Recommended Abundant Talent, but declined every appointment.

s0243.literal: Qiu took in marriage Shi Jian's niece's daughter, cast her aside; Jian took it as resentment, hinted to provinces, commanderies, and ducal offices not to summon him; therefore Xi and others for a long time could not be transferred.
s0243.idiomatic: Qiu married a niece of Shi Jian, then cast her off; Jian nursed a grudge and quietly blocked provincial and capital offices from employing the brothers, so Xi and Qiu went years without posts.

s0244.literal: In Taikang, within the commandery border great drought; Xi for the townsmen prayed for rain; in three days rain poured; the crowd said Xi's sincerity moved them; they made a song saying: "Mr. Shu, penetrates spirits and gods; prayed to Heaven three days, sweet rain falls."
s0244.idiomatic: During Taikang a severe drought struck the commandery; Xi led the townspeople in a rain prayer, and after three days a soaking rain fell. The people credited his sincerity and sang, "Master Shu moves the spirits—three days of prayer, and sweet rain descends from heaven."

s0245.literal: Our millet thereby is nurtured; our glutinous thereby is born.
s0245.idiomatic: Our crops revive; our grain springs up again.

s0248.literal: Xi with Wei Heng were thick and good; hearing Heng met disaster, from his native commandery he went to the mourning.
s0248.idiomatic: Xi was close to Wei Heng; on learning of Heng's violent death he hurried from his home commandery to attend the funeral.

s0249.literal: Once he composed the Exhorting Agriculture and Cake various rhapsodies; the text was rather vulgar; people of the time despised them.
s0249.idiomatic: He once wrote rhapsodies such as Exhorting Farming and On Cakes; the pieces were coarse in style and drew condescension from contemporaries.

s0250.literal: But his nature was submerged and retiring; he did not admire glory and profit; he made Explaining the Abstruse Dwelling to pattern after The Guest's Reproach; its phrases say:
s0250.idiomatic: By temperament he was retiring and indifferent to rank and gain; he composed The Rationale of Secluded Living in imitation of The Guest's Objections, which begins:

s0251.literal: Shu Xi dwelt in leisure; disciples together attended.
s0251.idiomatic: Shu Xi lived at leisure, his disciples in attendance.

s0252.literal: Just then lowering the curtain deep in talk, leaning on the armrest and laughing, holding a brush scattering pattern, examining and composing similarities and differences; one beside advanced and asked him, saying: "We have heard the Way esteems change and penetration; the perspicacious have no limit.
s0252.idiomatic: He had lowered his curtain for a searching discussion, leaned on the low table with a chuckle, poised his brush and scattered fine phrases as he weighed rival views. A disciple stepped forward: "We are told the Way prizes adaptability, and the wise see no final limit.

s0253.literal: Age chaotic then they save its tangle; times peaceful then they support its height.
s0253.idiomatic: In troubled times they untie the knot of chaos; in peace they help sustain a flourishing age.

s0254.literal: They raise heaven's net to assist the hundred affairs; they brighten the Emperor's burden and beat the imperial wind.
s0254.idiomatic: They shore up the pillars of state and further every task of government, brighten the Son of Heaven's enterprise, and fan the imperial virtue abroad.

s0255.literal: Living, then the whole territory joys in his existence; dead, then the realm within grieves his end.
s0255.idiomatic: In life the land rejoices in them; in death the world mourns their passing.

s0256.literal: Therefore the gentleman bends himself and stretches the Way; is not ashamed to stem the times.
s0256.idiomatic: Hence the noble man bows his person to exalt the Way and does not scorn to meet the needs of the hour.

s0257.literal: Supreme states have the saying 'without seeking how obtain'; the Changes shows leaping to seek advance's wording.
s0257.idiomatic: The great polities say, 'Seek not, gain not,' and the Book of Changes urges 'leaping' as the path to advancement.

s0258.literal: The old man of Shen bore the metal crossbar to set forth cutting-and-cooking discourse; a Qi guest faced the great crossroad and sang the White Water poem.
s0258.idiomatic: The elder of Shen shouldered ritual vessels to expound the butcher's art, while a visitor to Qi chanted White Water in the open street.

s0259.literal: Now you, sir, drown in the Way and cultivate arts, stand tall like a mountain, hidden brightness penetrates the subtle, harmoniously peruse deep knowledge, night joins forgetting-sleep's toil, day gallops boring-into-mystery's thought, empty years pile up years, you do not fall from your aim.
s0259.idiomatic: Yet you, sir, steep yourself in the Way and polish your arts, stand like a silent peak, your hidden insight probes the subtle, your reading runs deep, you toil nights without thought of sleep and spend days probing mysteries, year on year, never swerving from your purpose.

s0260.literal: Scales and wings complete yet more you crouch; craft and learning excellent yet not tried.
s0260.idiomatic: Though your talent has grown fins and feathers, you bury it deeper; though your learning surpasses others, you refuse to test it in office.

s0261.literal: Then you desire to shut the box and decline price, mud-coil in a deep place, forever sheathe luster of fine jade, hide head in the islet of exhausted fish; facing Tang years you admire Changju, state having the Way you reverse toward Ningwu.
s0261.idiomatic: You would lock away your talents like jewels in a casket, lie coiled in the mud, forever dim the gleam of your gifts, and hide like a spent fish in a shoal—envying Changju under the sage kings of Yao and Shun, yet imitating Ningwu when the realm is well governed.

s0262.literal: To know that and be lost on this—stupid I privately do not take.
s0262.idiomatic: To praise that course while blundering on this—such folly I cannot accept.

s0263.literal: As for gentlemen by pull ascending, advance must await seeking; when parties attached to power are promoted across the board, then forest-and-marsh's outstanding men are not drawn forth; vermillion steps walk silk-boasting boys; eastern wilds leave white-headed old men.
s0263.idiomatic: When office goes only to the well-connected and promotion waits on solicitation, cliques of the powerful monopolize advancement while recluses of talent stay hidden—boys in silks swagger up the palace stairs while white-haired worthies are left in the eastern wilds.

s0264.literal: Why not also rely on the capital and serve the Marquis of Bolu, borrow goose prow to cross the rushing current, tread emerald clouds to startle roaming dragons, shake radiance to alarm sunken loach?
s0264.idiomatic: Why not seize your moment at court, ride the wake of a Huo Guang, skim the flood on a high prow, tread the clouds to rouse soaring dragons, and flash your light to stir the depths?

s0265.literal: In vain you coil in a pitfall, gaze at heaven's road and do not roam; learning already piled yet the body trapped—what do you do in a secret hill?
s0265.idiomatic: Why coil in a snare, eyes on the high road yet never walking it—learning heaped up while the man stays stuck? What is the use of a hermit's hill?

s0266.literal: Moreover the years do not wait for me; the seasons are like galloping teams; they come and do not return; hard to obtain, easy to lose.
s0266.idiomatic: Time does not wait; the seasons race like chariots—what comes does not return, hard to win and easy to lose.

s0267.literal: Sir, do you not know the omen of yu-yu's regret for lateness, and forget the duty of friends-together's haste for speed—how then can you climb the sea's margin and dam the eastward-flowing water, stand by the Yu spring and beckon the west-returning sun?
s0267.idiomatic: Sir, do you miss the lesson of dithering until regret is too late, and ignore how allies must act with speed—do you think you can stand at the ocean's edge and stem the eastern tide, or by a sunless pool summon the setting sun back west?

s0268.literal: In vain you take crooked fear as fetters, Confucian learning self-shackles, imprison the great Way within a ringed wall, bitterly shape the body in a thatched room.
s0268.idiomatic: You let needless fear bind you, let book learning become your cage, lock the great Way inside a cramped lane, and torment your frame in a mean hut.

s0269.literal: How does that compare to entrusting the body to power and kin, borrowing force from position, choosing roost in fragrant woods, flying without awaiting wings, evening lodging in the rooms of the seven beauties, morning enjoying the food of five tripods, rectifying the three norms then the Grand Step is level, assisting the five teachings then the jade cord is straight?
s0269.idiomatic: Better to shelter under great houses, ride influence and borrowed strength, perch in the high forest, soar without waiting for wings, sup in mansions of delight, feast from bronze vessels, set the three norms aright so the stairway of state is level, and further the five teachings so the celestial cord hangs true—

s0270.literal: Who compares to eating bean-leaves and coarse greens, to the end concealing oneself!"
s0270.idiomatic: who would rather gnaw herbs in hiding for life?"

s0272.literal: I will guide you with the gentleman's Way, instruct you in the affairs of emerging and dwelling.
s0272.idiomatic: I shall set before you the way of the gentleman and explain what it means to serve or to withdraw.

s0273.literal: You there, brightly receive my questioning; carefully listen to my intent.
s0273.idiomatic: Listen closely to my questions and attend carefully to what I mean to say.

s0274.literal: Formerly the Primordial One already opened, the Two Forms began to stand; Li's light hid at night, the Moon-charioteer folded by day; feathered tribes soar in forests; caterpillars and larvae hurry to damp; things follow what nature settles in; gentlemen delight in what ambition grasps; some turn back from rich glory to dwell on cliffs; some push aside orchid gates to seek entry; those in the wilds are dragons in flight; those at court are phoenixes gathered.
s0274.idiomatic: When primordial unity first opened and yin and yang took shape, the sun hid its light at night and the moon yielded the day to birds winging through the woods and worms hastening to moisture—each creature follows its nature, each gentleman his chosen aim. Some spurn splendor for a life on the crags; others thrust aside palace gates to enter service. Recluses are dragons in flight; courtiers are phoenixes alighting.

s0275.literal: Although their tracks differ, in the Way there is no noble or base; they must pacify their occupation; they mutually do not envy; Ji and Qi rose to employments to proclaim the Way; Chao and You washed ears to avoid yielding the throne; together they hang the title of imperishable; both enter the stream of the worthy.
s0275.idiomatic: Their paths diverge, yet in the Way itself there is no high or low—each must rest content in his calling and not covet another's. Ji and Qi took office to spread the teaching; Chao and You washed their ears rather than accept the throne—both won an undying name and both rank among the worthy.

s0276.literal: Join names and compare reputations—who is inferior, who is superior?
s0276.idiomatic: Set name beside name and fame beside fame—who falls short, who excels?

s0277.literal: Why must one be greedy to be grouped with the two-eight, and ashamed to be a mate of the seven men!
s0277.idiomatic: Why crave a place among the eight sage ministers and scorn standing with the seven recluses!

s0278.literal: Moreover the Way parts yet penetrates; gentlemen do not share one inclination; I privately stitch myself to the tail conduct of those who dwell in retirement; I dare not hear your high analogy; I am about to ignore the rush-wheeled summons and not glance at it—what then is this talk of attaching to power and kin!
s0278.idiomatic: The Way may fork yet still meet; men of worth need not share one taste. I count myself among the humblest recluses and cannot accept your lofty comparison—I would pass by even a coach sent in earnest summons—so what is this about clinging to the mighty?

s0279.literal: Formerly Zhou and Han middle declined; the times were hard to entrust oneself to; omens of blessing already opened, openings of disaster also arose; morning they roamed towering palaces, evening they fell into jagged ravines; daytime laugh, night sigh; morning flower, evening fall; loyalty was not sufficient to guard oneself; disaster could not be measured beforehand; therefore gentlemen shunned ascending court and raced to forest and thicket.
s0279.idiomatic: When Zhou and Han slid into decline, the age was treacherous: good fortune opened its door, but calamity waited too—men who breakfasted in lofty halls might sup in jagged gorges, laughing by day and groaning by night, blooming at dawn and withering at dusk. Loyalty could not shield you; disaster struck without warning. That is why men of honor shunned the capital and fled to the wilds.

s0280.literal: Some destroyed name and defiled themselves; some did not eat their salaries; compare it to taking office from the casketed tortoise; liken holding office to the calf at suburban temples; Gongsun wept tears and declined the chancellorship; Yang Xiong raised argument against the red-clan.
s0280.idiomatic: Some ruined their good name to save their skins; others refused stipends from a discredited throne—no better than letting a temple tortoise choose your career, or like the sacrificial calf led to the suburban altars. Gongsun Hong wept as he declined the chancellorship; Yang Xiong spoke out against courting the executioner's axe.

s0281.literal: Now the great Jin is bright and high; the six harmonies are tranquil and still.
s0281.idiomatic: Today Great Jin flourishes in peace; the realm within the four seas is calm.

s0282.literal: Hornets and scorpions stop venom; bears and brown bears cease fierceness; the five punishments are not used; the eight cords are fully ordered; the lord has no arrogant excess's anger; ministers have no yak-tail tassel's requests; above and below mutually are at peace; they follow ritual and follow the Way.
s0282.idiomatic: Stings of malice are stilled, the fierceness of bears is checked, punishments lie unused, and the far reaches are ordered; the ruler does not rage at whim, ministers do not angle for dangling tassels of rank; high and low dwell in harmony under rite and principle.

s0283.literal: The court nurtures the beast that gores the crooked; the courtyard has the grass that points at flattery; disaster and execution can be escaped by loyalty; favor and salary can be preserved by compliance.
s0283.idiomatic: The court keeps the straight-horned beast that gores the wicked, and the courtyard grows the plant that betrays sycophants—loyalty wards off ruin, and orderly conduct secures honor and pay.

s0284.literal: Moreover, for advancing without perilous fear, while only taking stillness's tasks—such follows his nature.
s0284.idiomatic: Besides, to advance without dread of danger yet cleave to a life of quiet—that is simply following one's nature.

s0285.literal: When both can both be right, yet abandoning that and rushing to this—such follows his will.
s0285.idiomatic: When either course may be justified, yet one turns from that and chooses this—that is following one's own bent.

s0286.literal: In general non-action can untie the realm's below's tangles; blandness can save the state's urgency; those in position have affairs that reach exhaustion; those who set forth plans have words that do not enter; Di Huang could not turn back the western neighbor's raiders; Ping and Bo could not rectify Ruyi's installation; Ganmu lay down and Qin armies withdrew; the Four Hoary Ones rose and Lady Qi wept.
s0286.idiomatic: Nonaction can unravel the empire's knots; quiet simplicity can meet a state's crisis. Even those in power meet limits; even good counsel may not get a hearing. Di Huang could not stop the raid from the west; Chen Ping and Zhou Bo could not set the heir-apparent question right; Duan Ganmu stayed in bed and the Qin host drew back; the Four Hoary Ones came forth and Lady Qi wept her doom.

s0287.literal: If it is thus, what abandoning what grasping, what going what approaching?
s0287.idiomatic: Given that, what is there to renounce or cling to, to flee or pursue?

s0288.literal: Calling the forest on a mountain peak fragrant, calling the weeds at the valley bottom stinking.
s0288.idiomatic: You call a grove on the heights fragrant and rank growth in the hollows foul—

s0289.literal: Guarding allotment and following nature, only Heaven grants; birds do not borrow armor from tortoises; fish do not borrow feet from beasts; why must one laugh at Guzhu's poverty and envy Duke Jing of Qi's wealth!
s0289.idiomatic: yet each keeps his portion and follows his endowment—birds do not borrow shells from turtles, fish do not borrow legs from beasts. Why mock the poor integrity of the Guzhu brothers and covet the riches of Duke Jing of Qi?

s0290.literal: Ashamed of plain cloth thereby to give free rein to intent; rather patterned hide and trailing embroidery.
s0290.idiomatic: Better to feel shame in plain cloth while following your heart than to trail embroidered furs in moral compromise.

s0291.literal: Moreover if one can restrain one's person, then a dan-shi store becomes abundant;
s0291.idiomatic: Keep the body in check, and a modest granary feels full;

s0292.literal: if one wantonly releases one's desires, then Hailing's piled stores are not sufficient;
s0292.idiomatic: give free rein to appetite, and even the granaries of Hailing would not suffice;

s0293.literal: those who preserve the Way and power, then the body of a common man can be glorious;
s0293.idiomatic: hold fast to virtue, and a commoner's life shines bright;

s0294.literal: those who forget the great human relationships, then even the lord of ten thousand chariots still is disgraced.
s0294.idiomatic: forget the great bonds of humanity, and even a ruler of ten thousand chariots stands dishonored.

s0295.literal: I will grind the six canons to instruct the age, guard stillness and blandness to press down the vulgar, pair with Zheng the old at the sea's corner, match Yan the elder in remote Shu.
s0295.idiomatic: I mean to study the Six Classics to instruct the world, keep to quiet simplicity to steady common ways, and keep company with old Zheng by the shore and recluse Yan in distant Shu.

s0296.literal: Moreover, taking the Grand Void as carriage, the dark furnace as market, spirit roams in the forest of none who rival, mind dwells in the chamber of none who schemes; glory and profit do not disturb his waking, deep sorrow does not interfere with his sleep; he casts away what boasters crave, gathers what restless affairs discard; clears the wilderness of the sage canons, gathers the crowd of words to one arrival.
s0296.idiomatic: I would take boundless void for my chariot and the hidden forge for my stall, roam in tracts where no rival intrudes, and lodge where no schemes stir—unmoved by gain in waking hours, untroubled by care in sleep, leaving to the vain what they chase, reclaiming what the frantic cast aside, clearing the neglected ground of the classics, and bringing many voices to a single insight.

s0297.literal: He completes plain walking in hill and garden, turns back tassel-cords and long flees; you, sir, examine my occupation in a thousand years; do not listen to my words today."
s0297.idiomatic: I would keep plain integrity in field and grove, turn my back on official cords, and wander far—judge my life's work a millennium hence, not by what I say today."

s0298.literal: Zhang Hua saw it and deemed him strange.
s0298.idiomatic: Zhang Hua read it and was struck by his talent.

s0299.literal: When Shi Jian died, Wang Rong then summoned Qiu.
s0299.idiomatic: After Shi Jian died, Wang Rong at last offered Qiu a post.

s0300.literal: Hua summoned Xi to be a retainer; moreover he was summoned by the Minister of Works, Prince of Xiapi, Huang.
s0300.idiomatic: Zhang Hua appointed Xi as a clerk, and he was also recruited by Prince Huang of Xiapi, who held the post of Minister of Works.

s0301.literal: When Hua became Minister of Works, again he made him Banditry Section subordinate.
s0301.idiomatic: When Zhang Hua became Minister of Works, he again named Xi an aide in the section for bandit suppression.
